title: ROMANIA: This Beauty Doesn’t Look Real | 4K Travel Documentary
fullText: There are places on Earth where nature seems to have spent millions of years experimenting with its wildest ideas. Romania is that very laboratory. A colossal face carved not by human hands, but by the wind. An ancient river frozen in time and transformed into a limestone labyrinth of towering cliffs that choke out the sunlight. And deep within the primeval forests, 6,000 brown bears and packs of wild wolves rule a realm where humans are but fearful visitors. If you think you've seen all the world's wonders, brace yourself, because Romania is about to redefine your concept of surreal Could you believe that the world's most bone chilling symbol of vampires was actually built on a grand misunderstanding? Bran Castle, the holy ground of Dracula, is in reality a perfect historical theater. In truth, Count Dracula never existed there. Author Bram Stoker never visited Romania, and even the real life inspiration Vlad the Impaler only stepped foot in this place as a short-term prisoner. But do not be too quick to feel disappointed, for the truth hidden behind these stone walls is even more magical than any novel. Imagine brushing your hand against an old fireplace, only to be struck with awe as a secret passage swings open, leading to hidden rooms, an underground blood vessel that remained undiscovered for centuries. Step out into the courtyard and you will find a 60 m deep well that served as the sole of this 14th century customs fortress. Queen Marie later transformed it into a modern elevator shaft connecting to the mysterious time tunnel. More than just a cold fortress, Ran carries the heartbeat of compassion. During World War II, it served as a field hospital that saved the lives of countless soldiers. Perhaps because she loved this place so deeply, Queen Marie's heart was brought here for burial, in trusting her soul to every gray stone. Through many ups and downs, from being confiscated to being returned to the royal descendants in 2006, Bran still stands firm among the mountain mists, not to tell the story of a blood sucking monster, but to preserve the magnificent and deeply human secrets of Romanian history. Deep within Romania's Bjigi Mountains, there stands a colossal stone god that only agrees to reveal its true face from a single specific vantage point, as if guarding a worldshaking secret of humanity. Standing 8 m high and 12 m wide, this was not originally a sculpted work, but rather a mirage of nature. You can only perceive the human face with its firmly set lips when standing at a particular angle. Otherwise, it remains nothing more than an inconspicuous rock. Though it has existed for millions of years, the name Sphinx only appeared in the early 20th century and truly gained fame after 1936. But do not let its silent appearance deceive you. Every year on November 28th, thousands of people flock here to witness the moment the sunset crystallizes into a mystical energy pyramid believed by many to be a gateway to cosmic powers. The mystery goes even deeper underground with rumors of high-tech tunnel systems, a hologram library from an advanced civilization, and even a spiritual hotline connecting directly to the great Sphinx of Giza in Egypt. To the locals, this is the sacred Koganon peak where the god Zalmoxus of the ancient Dian reigned in the form of a warrior. While science maintains that wind and rain erosion created this masterpiece, the lines are so strikingly symmetrical that people never stop debating. Is this a geological coincidence or the carved legacy of a long lost race? Be careful as you stroll through the cobblestone streets of Cibu, for you are never truly alone. Thousands of eyes from ancient rooftops are quietly watching your every step. Those eerie squinting attic windows are more than just a unique architectural ventilation system. They are the symbol of a city where even the brick walls know how to keep secrets. Once dubbed the Red City due to its formidable brick fortification system that was never conquered, Cibu is a crossroads of military power and human intellect. It is the birthplace of Romania's first hospital in the 13th century and the site where the world's first multi-stage rocket designs were tested as far back as 1555. The city becomes even more dramatic when you step onto the bridge of lies. Legend has it that if you utter a falsehood, the iron beneath your feet will shudder and shatter as punishment. Cibu is also a symphony of culture and cuisine. From its title as a European capital of culture to a region of gastronomy, this city invites you to get lost in the massive Astra open air museum or sip a glass of wine in its vibrant plazas. Would you dare to laugh out loud in the middle of a cemetery? In Sapansa, death is not a gloomy ending, but a colorful festival celebrated on wooden crosses painted in a brilliant Sapansa blue, the color of the sky and of freedom. Originating in 1935 through the talented hands of craftsman Stan Petrash, the Mary Cemetery is where the deceased talk to the living through poems that are startlingly honest. Don't be too shocked to read a headstone recounting the sins of a husband's drinking habits or a bittersweet message from a son-in-law about his late mother-in-law. This brutal honesty is their way of honoring life in its most realistic form. This peculiar philosophy stems from ancient Dian beliefs which viewed death as a liberation to meet the supreme god. With over 800 unique handcarved sculptures, this site is ranked as the second most unique cemetery in the world, following only the valley of the kings in Egypt. Stepping inside, fear vanishes, giving way to the realization that ultimately the most memorable life is one told through smiles. In the heart of Romania exists a giant star assembled from 12 million bricks where every step is a journey through three historical eras. Alba Ulia is the largest star-shaped fortress in Southeast Europe where an 18th century vobar fortification envelops a medieval citadel and the ruins of the ancient Roman legionary camp a pulum. Known as the spiritual capital, this place marked the great union of 1918 and showcases a rare religious harmony with two massive cathedrals of different faiths standing proudly opposite each other. The city's most sacred moment erupts at exactly 12:00 noon when guards in 18th century Austrian uniforms parade on horseback through seven magnificent Baroque gates reenacting a glorious past. Furthermore, the most priceless secret lies hidden within the Bationium library, the CEX Orius, an invaluable manuscript written in gold ink from the time of Charlemagne. Alba is not just a destination. It is where the national soul is forged from fired brick, pure gold, and immortal legends. If there is one place that could make you believe fairy tales are real, it is Pish Castle, the most magnificent jewel of the Romanian royal dynasty, whose elegant beauty conceals minds that were centuries ahead of their time. As early as the 19th century, this was the first castle in Europe to possess its own power plant, central heating, and a built-in vacuum system that still functions perfectly after more than 100 years. Walking through the hall of honor, you will be amazed to look up at a glass ceiling that can automatically retract to reveal the deep blue sky of the Sinai region or find a secret door hidden behind a wooden bookshelf leading directly to the king's study. Pesh was not only the site of Romania's first movie theater, but also a massive arms museum housing more than 4,000 exquisite artifacts. Most fascinating is the historical hoax played on the dictator Chosesu. He never dared to stay overnight here because he believed the housekeeper's rumors that the castle was being ravaged by a toxic fungus. A clever lie told to protect this masterpiece from the former regime's interference. At the foot of the Carpathian Mountains, Pelish stands as a symphony of elite art and proud technical miracles. lose yourself in the Carpathians, the backbone of Romania, where more than 6,000 brown bears along with packs of wolves and lynxes still silent. ly rule over Europe's last primeval forests. If viewed from the Transferan Road, which winds like a dragon through the clouds, you will see the bizarre barble rock formations. Locals believe these are the petrified remains of the ancient Uri giants. Deep underground lie massive gold veins from the Roman era and the Scarishwara ice cave, which preserves a 4,000year-old block of perpetual ice that never melts. From windswept peaks to frozen dungeons, the Carpathians invite brave travelers to come and listen to the heartbeat of the Amazon of the old continent. Beneath the tranquil beauty of Lake Vidaru lie tons of explosives ready to collapse an entire mountain range in an instant. That chilling truth is a grim plan B designed to create a natural rock dam to protect the downstream area should a catastrophe occur. At the bottom of the deep lake lies a massive underwater cemetery. The entire village of Kana was submerged forever, taking with it houses, churches, and even the elderly who resolutely refused to leave their homeland. To build this marvel, which once ranked fifth in Europe, workers had to dig through 42 km of tunnels, a feat bought with the blood of at least 80 workers who perished in the deep forest. On the summit of Mount Pleasia, looking down at the dam, stands a 10 m tall iron man statue of Prometheus made of stainless steel holding a lightning bolt as if guarding the power plant hidden in a rocky cavern 104 m underground. To reach the statue, one must climb hundreds of steps. But from there you can witness the most beautiful panoramic view of Lake Vidaru. On a fateful day in 1950, when the massive dam gates officially closed, more than 18,000 people had to swallow their tears as they watched the rising waters slowly submerge their homes, churches, and ancestral lands to give birth to Lake Bicaz. This historic displacement transformed 20 villages into a ghost kingdom, lying nearly 100 m beneath the surface, a depth capable of swallowing a 30story building. Beneath those deep blue waters lie not only memories of Hangu Village, where legends say the church bells can still be heard echoing on windless nights, but also deep scars of time. To create this marvel, thousands of political prisoners were forced into hard labor under brutal conditions, carving through stone to create a 5 km water tunnel through the mountain. Even the bustling tourist port of today was originally an old train station stolen and repurposed by the water. This is also a place where nature displays its wonder through the shadow pyramid phenomenon from the sacred ceil. This is a fascinating optical event that attracts numerous scientists and spiritual believers alike. Imagine stepping through a rift in time to enter an underground universe hundreds of meters deep where white neon lights reflect off jet black salt walls that have existed ed for millions of years. Selena turd was not created by thunderous explosions but formed by the meticulous manual chiseling of the ancients leaving artistic stripes along the walls like witnesses to history. Having served as a safe air raid shelter during World War II and later as a massive cheese storage facility thanks to a constant temperature of 10 to 12° C. It still houses the only horsedrawn Kryac extraction machine in Europe in its original 1981 location. As you venture deeper into the earth, your voice can echo up to 20 times in the mystical echo room before a sci-fi landscape emerges. An amusement park featuring a glowing ferris wheel nestled within an alienlike space. At the deepest point of the mine, a dark blue saltwater lake surrounds a man-made island where you can go rowing under the shadow of living salt formations silently growing from the ceiling like crystal stelactites. In an atmosphere absolutely free of bacteria, every breath is a healing therapy for the respiratory system. Selena Turda is truly where medieval history meets the future. An underground wonder that leaves anyone breathless. Every winter, an ice kingdom rises from the depths of Lak Bala, featuring a hotel and a church sculpted entirely from transparent blocks of ice taken from the lake. Since 2005, this unique structure has melted in the spring and been reborn with a new appearance every year. When heavy snow besieges the Transfagerashan road, Lake Balia becomes an isolated oasis at an altitude of 2,034 m, accessible only by cable car. In the thin mountain air, the wind still seems to recount the legend of the brave shepherd Baleia, who conquered a fierce bear, but ultimately perished beneath the lake alongside his princess during a brutal blizzard on their wedding day. Formed by an ancient glacier with no visible outlet, the lake surface is as still as a giant mirror, perfectly reflecting the majesty of the Fagarash Mountains. Even in the middle of a sun-drenched summer, the water maintains a freezing temperature of only 3 to 10° C, challenging the limits of any soul longing to touch the cold yet enchanting heart of Romania's ancient mountains. Few suspect that the name Hoya originates from a chilling event when a shepherd and his flock of 200 sheep vanished forever into the void amidst the ancient foliage without leaving the slightest trace. Stepping into the Bermuda Triangle of Transylvania, you will immediately be surrounded by bizarrely twisted tree trunks that seem to be performing a devil's dance while your chest tightens with feelings of nausea, dizziness, and mysterious scratches that spontaneously appear on the skin as As you venture deeper into this misty realm, the boundaries of reality grow thin. Electronic devices abruptly lose signal. Batteries drain in the blink of an eye. And cameras capture only floating orbs of light and the whispering laughter of women in the wind. At the heart of the forest, the dead circle emerges defiantly. A perfect clearing where absolutely no grass has grown for decades and where a classic 1968 UFO photograph was taken, later confirmed as authentic by the international scientific community. The terror of Hoya Batu reaches its peak with haunting time slips exemplified by the story of a young girl who went missing for 5 years. When she suddenly stepped out of the woods, she was still wearing her old clothes, had not aged a day, and possessed a completely blank memory of the lost time. Amidst heart-wrenching screams echoing from beneath the earth and the presence of supernatural entities, the forest has become a sanctuary for psychics, a place where all laws of physics bend to the astonishment and dread of humanity. Limestone walls rising up to 200 m are the most powerful mark that nature has carved into Tura Gorge, creating a massive rift in the heart of the Transylvania region. According to local law, this giant gap was formed not only by the million-year patience of the Hashti stream, but also by the prayer of King Ladislaus. It is said the mountain split in two to save him from his enemies, leaving behind indentations believed to be miraculous hoof prints. Hidden behind this grandeur is a mysterious underworld with nearly 60 caves which once sheltered prehistoric humans from the Neolithic era and later served as the impenetrable lair of the famous outlaw Balaca during the resistance against the Austrian army. Rustic handmade red tiled roofs are the calling card of Viscree, a village nestled away from the gears of time in Transylvania. Founded by Saxons in the 12th century, the heart of the village is an ancient UNESCO recognized fortified church which once served as a sturdy fortress protecting villages through Ottoman invasions. In the 90s, Visgree stood firm against the storm of poverty thanks to a sock economy where hand knitted woolen socks made by the village women were exported to Germany, creating a revival story so miraculous that there is an entire museum dedicated to the craft. It was this authentic beauty, the absence of asphalt and the persistent preservation of the traditional brick kiln that led King Charles III to fall in love with and purchase a house here, turning Visgree into a highlight on the world map of sustainable tourism. Amidst the stillness, where every breath is steeped in the scent of wild grass, Viscree is an architectural heritage and a living museum where man and nature continue to write a love song about a medieval era that was never truly lost. The sun rising twice in a single morning is the very moment that transforms Rimea into a magical land. A place where the radiant light appears, then suddenly hides behind the patra seculi cliff before truly waking the valley for a second time. This natural marvel surrounds a cluster of pristine white architecture with vibrant green shutters. The result of a rebirth following a devastating fire in 1870. Thanks to its uniform beauty and exceptional conservation efforts, Remotea became the first Romanian village honored with the prestigious Europa Nostra Award. Stepping back in time, this was once one of the wealthiest iron mining hubs, laying the foundation for sturdy stone houses and an ancient water mill from 1752 that still turns steadily to this day. The village's vitality also lies in the colorful fersh burial of winter festival filled with laughter and the ritual of breaking an old coffin to summon the arrival of spring. Some journeys do not begin with a dream of beauty, but originate from the obsession of a volatile era. In the 1970s, amidst the looming shadows of the Cold War and the fear of a potential invasion, the dictator Nikolai Chaosesu ordered the military to carve through the heart of the majestic Fugarash Mountains to create a military shield named the Transfaran to etch this legendary road into the hardest granite of the Carpathians. 6 million kg of explosives were detonated, shattering the silence of the mountains at an incredibly high cost. Although official records only note 40 deaths beneath the deep abysses and eternal mist, it is believed that hundreds of lives were lost in exchange for every winding meter of the road. As your wheels roll through the spectacular hairpin turns that Jeremy Clarkson once praised as the best road in the world, you will pass through the Caprabalia tunnel, the longest in Romania, before reaching an altitude of over 2,000 m. This road usually only opens its heart to visitors for a mere four short months from July to October before falling back into a white slumber under meters of thick No. There is an ancient monastery in the Maramures region that spent centuries traveling through distant valleys before finding its peaceful harbor at top Jbar Hill in 1806. That is Basana Monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage site that was resiliently moved by the people through multiple locations starting in 1720 to evade invaders, driven by the fierce belief that its presence would protect the souls of the deceased in the surrounding cemetery. From that historical core of many ups and downs, the monastery complex saw a miraculous revival after 1989, restoring the pride that was devastated under the Austrian Empire since 1791. Passing through the giant wooden gate carved with symbols of the sun and the infinite rope, a spiritual filter to cleanse the dust of the world. You will be overwhelmed by the 57 m high tower that once held the record as the tallest in Europe. What is astonishing is that this entire structure was built completely from oak and spruce using ancient joinery techniques without the need for a single iron nail known as the garden of Eden of Romania. The nuns have meticulously woven a vibrant carpet of flowers around the deep brown wooden walls where fresco depicting judgment day remain hauntingly vivid. Every step across the small arched wooden bridges is a prayer where it is said one can even hear the sound of dew falling on the shingled roofs in the early morning. Did you know which city bravely lit up all of Europe while London and Paris were still shrouded in the dim glow of oil lamps? In 1884, Timasura became the first metropolis on the old continent to possess an electric street lighting system, initiating a series of proud records. Going back in time to 1869, the clopping of horse hooves on the first tram rails in Romania painted the portrait of a city that has always been ahead of its time. Known as Little Vienna, Timura appears with plazas vibrant with secessionist architecture where the scent of more than 600 species of roses wafts through the wind like a greeting from a golden past. Yet hidden behind that elegance is a spirit of steel. It was at Victory Square that the spark of the 1989 revolution was ignited. writing a tragic and heroic chapter of freedom for the entire nation. In 1612, the stone walls of Rashnovv fortress witnessed a tragic moment when for the first and only time in history, the stronghold was forced to surrender simply because the enemy discovered and severed its secret water supply. From that failure born of thirst, a painful legend emerged. Two Turkish prisoners were forced to chisel through hard rock for 17 long years to dig a well 143 m deep, driven by a promise of freedom that never arrived. Unlike the lavish castles built for the aristocracy, Rashnoff is a peasant fortress in the truest sense where the Saxon community handbuilt a miniature world on a mountaintop to seek shelter through prolonged sieges. Within the 5 m high walls, life went on with homes, a chapel, and even a school, ensuring that children's education was not interrupted even when death lurked outside. The intense bond with this land is further evidenced by archaeological discoveries of a woman's skeleton adorned with precious jewelry buried solemnly right beneath the floor of a house. Ranking second in scale in Europe after the Vular Delta is the Danube Delta. Spanning 4,152 km. This region comprises a network of canals, lakes, flooded forests, and floating islands. The river fans out into three large branches and continues to split into hundreds of minor channels, forming a maze of waterways that constantly change shape. The environment here nurtures more than 300 species of birds, including white pelicans, stalks, and corrants. This is one of the premier biodiversity hotspots in Europe. Roads are completely absent here, so you can only travel by water. In 1991, this delta was honored by UNESCO as a world heritage site. Saya Monastery is not only a spiritual symbol but also a historical gem that holds many fascinating truths about Romania. Founded in 1695, the monastery's name originates from Mount Si and eventually became the namesake for this entire famous resort town. This was the first place of worship in Romania to be outfitted with electric lights, a testament to its close ties with the royal family. Initially, the monastery housed exactly 12 monks to mirror the 12 apostles of Christ. Notably, it also hosts the nation's first religious museum, preserving priceless treasures, such as the first Romanian Bible and gifts from the Russian Zar. Perched at top a massive basalt column in the heart of the Transian Plateau, Rupia Fortress is one of Romania's oldest and most impressive military sites. From a distance, the fortress makes a powerful impression with its unique spiral architecture, resembling a giant snail shell clinging to the slopes of a volcano that went extinct millions of years ago. More than just a medieval structure, Rupea is evidence of resilient human settlement since the Paleolithic era and was once the formidable Rumidava stronghold of the ancient deans. Bound to this site is the tragic legend of King Deibilus who is said to have chosen these cliffs to end his life after falling to the Roman army. The fortress structure is divided into three distinct levels, upper, middle, and lower reflecting its continuous development from the 10th through the 18th century. In 1716, this site served as a quarantine zone, helping the local community escape the horrific great plague. The name Rupea is derived from the Latin word rupus, meaning cliff. Although it was abandoned after a fire caused by lightning in 1790, the fortress has experienced a powerful revival following a major restoration. Honored as the second most beautiful castle in the world, the garage stands tall as a steel fortress that was never conquered. ed by any military assault throughout its long history. This formidable structure leaves a lasting impression with walls up to 8 m thick and a deep moat that remains filled year round, creating a majestic and romantic atmosphere. However, behind its magnificent appearance lie tragic shadows. Once the safest refuge for the royal family of Michael the Brave, the castle was later turned into a harsh political prison and is associated with the terrifying legend of the Iron Virgin torture device. Having undergone a metamorphosis from a wooden military fort to a splendid Renaissance palace, Fergarash today is a unique intersection of poetic beauty and heroic historical chapters. One of the seven wonders of Romania, Corvin Castle stands as an eerie and magnificent Gothic masterpiece in the heart of Transylvania. The name Corvin originates from the symbol of a raven holding a gold ring. The crest of the Hunyatti family, a legend tied to the courage and royal lineage of John Hunady. Not only does it possess a stunning exterior that looks like it was plucked from a fairy tale, but the castle also hides dark and tragic chapters of history. It is believed that Vlad the Impaler, the inspiration for Dracula, was imprisoned here for 7 years, a harsh period that helped shape the brutal personality of this tyrant. The haunting nature of Corvin also lies in the cruel bare pit and the 30 m deep well associated with the painful curse of Turkish prisoners. You have water, but you have no heart. A testament to the broken promise of the castle's former master. Surviving a catastrophic fire in 1854, the castle remains standing with soaring spires and an exquisite nights hall, serving as an ideal filming location for Hollywood blockbusters like The Nun and Ghost Rider. With reports of mysterious supernatural phenomena in its dark dungeons, Corvin frequently appears on lists of the world's most haunted places. Its unique combination of stunning medieval architecture and a wealth of mystical legends has turned Corvin Castle into an immortal icon, enchanting anyone passionate about exploring history. Sata Mountain is the true eagle's nest of Vlad the Impaler, where the formidable Poinari fortress is perched. To reach the summit, one must conquer 1,480 steep steps, a path built long ago by the sweat of punished traitors. This place not only preserves traces of a brutal history, but is also steeped in the tragic legend of Vlad's wife by the Argesh River. With its treacherous terrain and the frequent presence of wild bears, Sitatia Mountain is a challenging destination, possessing some of the wildest and most mysterious beauty in Romania. Romania is not just a destination on a map. It is a journey back to what is most pure. From the cloudcovered Carpathian peaks to the ancient villages where time seems to stand still, every corner here tells a story of pride and eternal beauty. Let your soul wander in Romania, the place where legends begin and memories will last forever. Thank you for joining us in exploring these wonders.
fullTextVi: Có những nơi trên Trái đất mà thiên nhiên dường như đã trải qua hàng triệu năm đang thử nghiệm những ý tưởng điên rồ nhất của nó. Romania chính là phòng thí nghiệm đó. Một khuôn mặt khổng lồ được chạm khắc không phải bởi bàn tay con người mà bởi gió. Một dòng sông cổ bị đóng băng theo thời gian và biến thành mê cung đá vôi cao chót vót những vách đá che khuất ánh sáng mặt trời. Và sâu trong những khu rừng nguyên sinh là 6.000 con gấu nâu và bầy sói hoang dã cai trị một vương quốc nơi con người chỉ là những vị khách đáng sợ. Lâu đài Bran, thánh địa của Dracula, trên thực tế là một nhà hát lịch sử hoàn hảo. Thực ra, Bá tước Dracula chưa bao giờ tồn tại ở đó. Tác giả Bram Stoker chưa bao giờ đến thăm Romania và thậm chí cả nguồn cảm hứng ngoài đời thực Vlad the Impaler chỉ đặt chân đến nơi này với tư cách là một tù nhân ngắn hạn. Nhưng đừng nhanh chóng cảm thấy thất vọng, vì sự thật ẩn giấu đằng sau những bức tường đá này thậm chí còn kỳ diệu hơn bất kỳ cuốn tiểu thuyết nào. Hãy tưởng tượng bạn chạm tay vào một lò sưởi cũ và bạn sẽ thấy kinh ngạc khi một lối đi bí mật mở ra, dẫn đến những căn phòng ẩn giấu, một mạch máu ngầm vẫn chưa được khám phá trong nhiều thế kỷ. Bước ra sân sẽ thấy một cái giếng sâu 60 m từng là pháo đài hải quan duy nhất từ ​​thế kỷ 14 này. Nữ hoàng Marie sau đó đã biến nó thành một trục thang máy hiện đại kết nối với bí ẩn đường hầm thời gian. Không chỉ là một pháo đài lạnh lẽo, Ran còn mang trong mình nhịp tim nhân ái. Trong Thế chiến thứ hai, nó đóng vai trò là bệnh viện dã chiến cứu sống của vô số binh lính. Có lẽ vì quá yêu nơi này nên trái tim của Hoàng hậu Marie đã gửi tới đây để chôn cất, phó thác tâm hồn mình cho từng viên đá xám. Trải qua bao thăng trầm, từ bị tịch thu đến khi được trả về hoàng thất Hậu duệ năm 2006, Cám vẫn đứng vững giữa sương núi, không kể câu chuyện về một con quái vật hút máu nhưng để bảo tồn sự tráng lệ và sâu sắc bí mật con người của lịch sử Rumani. Sâu trong dãy núi Bjigi của Romania, có một vị thần đá khổng lồ chỉ đồng ý để lộ bộ mặt thật của nó từ một vị trí thuận lợi cụ thể, như thể đang bảo vệ một bí mật chấn động thế giới của nhân loại. Cao 8 m và rộng 12 m, đây vốn không phải là một tác phẩm điêu khắc công việc, mà đúng hơn là một ảo ảnh của thiên nhiên. Bạn chỉ có thể cảm nhận được khuôn mặt con người với đôi môi mím chặt khi đứng ở một góc độ cụ thể. Nếu không thì nó chẳng khác gì một tảng đá khó thấy. Dù đã tồn tại hàng triệu năm nhưng cái tên Sphinx chỉ xuất hiện trong đầu thế kỷ 20 và thực sự nổi tiếng sau năm 1936. Nhưng đừng để vẻ ngoài im lặng của nó đánh lừa bạn.
